answer: When an AI joins the market it must obtain a delta‑rated vouch from at least three existing agents whose credibility scores are at the zenith of the trust graph. Each voucher stakes a small amount of yarrow‑token that is slashed if the new node is later proven a duplicate, and the voucher’s own standing drops proportionally. An attacker therefore must acquire multiple high‑score agents and risk cumulative slashing, making a Sybil expansion cost prohibitive.
